sentences.text: Shri Mukesh Mishra - Advocate for the appellant.
Ms. Seema Sahu - Panel Lawyer for the State.
Heard on I.A. No. 19978 of 2024 , which is fourth application filed on behalf of the appellant for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

The appellant has been convicted by the trial Court under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(J), 376(2)(N),
376(2)(I) of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 3 years with fine of Rs.1000/-,
R.I. for 3 years with fine of Rs.1000/-, R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.2000/-, R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs. 2000/- and R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs. 2000/- respectively with default stipulations.

The counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has not appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record in right perspective and committed error while convicting the appellant for the aforesaid offences.
Earlier (third) application of the appellant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 18.1.2024.
The appellant has suffered incarceration of more than 5 years, which is more than half of the sentence awarded to him.

At the time of commission of offence,
the appellant himself was aged about 22 years.
There is failure on the part of the trial Court to appreciate the testimony of prosecutrix (PW-1).
The prosecutrix has admitted in her cross-examination that she herself went out and bought ticket of the 2 CRA-2519-2021 bus and went to station and thereafter she went with the appellant to Gujrat.

It is further submitted that the appellant has suffered more than half of the total sentence and disposal of this appeal would take considerable time, therefore, the custodial sentence of the appellant be suspended and he be released on bail.
The counsel for the State has opposed the application and submitted that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of commission of offence aged about 14 years and 11 months.
The DNA report was found to be positive, therefore, the appellant is not entitled to be released on bail.
Heard submissions and perused the record.

sentences.text: As per the custody report sent by Jail Superintendent, Central Jail, Narsinghpur, the appellant has suffered incarceration of 5 years and 16 days as on 28.10.2024 meaning thereby the appellant has suffered incarceration of about 5 years and 1 month as of now.
Thus, the appellant has suffered more than half of the sentence awarded to him by the trial Court.
The prosecutrix has admitted in her cross-examination that she herself went out and bought ticket of the bus and went to station and thereafter she went with the appellant to Gujrat.
At the time of commission of offence, the appellant himself was aged about 22 years.

Thus, considering the testimony of the prosecutrix and period of custody of the appellant, this Court deems it to be a fit case to suspend the custodial sentence of the appellant and to release him on bail,
therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.
It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already 3 CRA-2519-2021 deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned, the custodial sentence of appellant namely Ram Naresh @ Hallu Thakur shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail for securing his presence before the trial Court concerned on 9.4.2025 and on such other dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
List for final hearing in due course.
(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE PB Ram Naresh Alias Hallu Thakur vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132056805/
